fr_tassi.titolo: Annual Notice of Interest Rates for Fixed-Rate Federal Student Loans Made Under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program (91 FR 57581, September 10, 2026)
fr_tassi.chi: Federal Student Aid, U.S. Department of Education (Federal Register)

frasi.periodo: with first disbursement dates on or after July 1, 2026, and before July 1, 2027
frasi.fisso: The interest rate for these loans is a fixed rate that is determined annually for all loans first disbursed during any 12-month period beginning on July 1 and ending on June 30.
frasi.formula: The rate is equal to the high yield of the 10-year Treasury notes auctioned at the final auction held before June 1 of that 12-month period, plus a statutory add-on percentage that varies depending on the loan type and, for Direct Unsubsidized Loans, whether the loan was made to an undergraduate or graduate student.
frasi.massimo: If the interest rate formula results in a rate that exceeds the statutory maximum rate, the rate is the statutory maximum rate.
frasi.vita: the rate determined for any loan is a fixed interest rate for the life of the loan
frasi.asta: On May 12, 2026, the United States Treasury Department held a 10-year Treasury note auction that resulted in a high yield of 4.468 percent, rounded to 4.47 percent.
frasi.consolidamento: have a fixed interest rate that is equal to the weighted average of the interest rates on the loans consolidated, rounded to the nearest higher one-eighth of one percent
frasi.laureati: Graduate and professional students are not eligible to receive Direct Subsidized Loans.

fr_regola.titolo: Reimagining and Improving Student Education—Federal Student Loan Program Final Regulations; Final Rule (91 FR 23768, May 1, 2026)

frasi.vigore: This final rule is effective on July 1, 2026.
frasi.sintesi: These changes include establishing new loan limits for graduate students, professional students, and parents, and phasing out the Graduate PLUS (Grad PLUS) Program.
frasi.invariati: The undergraduate loan limits in Sec. 685.203 remain unchanged; the aggregate Subsidized and Unsubsidized loan limits for dependent and independent undergraduates are $31,000 and $57,500, respectively.
frasi.laureato: A graduate student, who is not a professional student, for a period of enrollment beginning on or after July 1, 2026, may borrow up to $20,500 for any academic year under the Direct Unsubsidized Loan Program.
frasi.professionale: A professional student, for a period of enrollment beginning on or after July 1, 2026, may borrow up to $50,000 for any academic year under the Direct Unsubsidized Loan Program.
frasi.genitori_anno: For periods of enrollment beginning on or after July 1, 2026, the total amount of all Direct PLUS Loans that all parents may borrow on behalf of each dependent student for any academic year of study may not exceed $20,000.
frasi.genitori_totale: For periods of enrollment beginning on or after July 1, 2026, the total amount of all Direct PLUS Loans that all parents may borrow on behalf of each dependent student may not exceed $65,000, without regard to any amounts repaid, forgiven, canceled, or otherwise discharged on any such loan.
frasi.vita: Effective July 1, 2026, the lifetime maximum aggregate amount of loans made, insured, or guaranteed under the Act that a student may borrow, shall be $257,500, excluding Federal Direct PLUS or Federal PLUS loans made to that student as a parent on behalf of another dependent undergraduate student.

frasi.minimo_10: A borrower's payments under this repayment plan are at least $50 per month, except that a borrower's final payment may be less than $50.
frasi.trasferimento: If a student transfers to a different institution, even in the same program of study, the Department would consider that to be a new program of study.
frasi.laureati_programma: Conversely, graduate students who change their program of study will be ineligible for the interim exception.

frasi.major: a student who changes majors within the same degree or certificate shall be considered to be enrolled in the same program of study.
